title: Empirical evaluation of work-to-force transition models and architectural coupling gate

de_poli_group_audit.scope_limitation: Restricted strictly to published group-level averages (Table 3). Individual continuous time-series data are available only upon author request (prohibited under project governance).

SIT_group.work_change_description: CWR power increased by +11.0% at unchanged time-to-task failure, yielding +8.5% to +11.0% greater external mechanical work in Joules.
SIT_group.explanation: Despite performing significantly more total mechanical work post-training, the SIT group exhibited higher force retention (+3.72 pp), refuting the monotonic scalar work-fatigue hypothesis.

control_group.work_change_description: CWR power -0.7%, duration unchanged, work approximately constant.

justifications: Out-of-sample failure: On held-out individual subjects (Norbury 12 men, paired LL and HL conditions), incorporating workload/volume into force prediction increased MAE by 4.08 N over a simple mean retention baseline (baseline MAE 50.61 N vs volume linear MAE 54.69 N; paired difference -4.08 N, 95% CI [-8.49, -0.29] N, strictly favoring baseline).

Directional failure: In de Poli et al., performing +8.5% to +11% more external mechanical work was accompanied by higher force retention (75.08% vs 71.36%), directly violating the assumption that force decrement monotonically tracks cumulative work.

Intensity domain omission: A scalar Joules ledger ignores whether work is performed below, at, or above Critical Power / Respiratory Compensation Point. Sub-CP work produces minimal force loss, whereas supra-CP work produces rapid exhaustion with limited total Joules.

Recovery latency neglect: Real post-exercise force measurements have an unmodeled delay (25 s in de Poli, 5 min in Norbury) during which rapid PCr resynthesis and central drive recovery occur. A static transition model cannot transfer across protocols.

Central vs peripheral confusion: Total work cannot be mapped directly to muscle contractile capacity without separating peripheral cross-bridge inhibition from motoneuronal voluntary activation failure.

proposed_reconstructed_transition_archit.state_1: Domain-partitioned mechanical demand (moderate vs heavy vs severe domain based on CP/RCP).
proposed_reconstructed_transition_archit.state_2: Bi-compartmental fatigue state: peripheral cross-bridge metabolite penalty (H+, Pi, PCr) + central voluntary activation deficit (%VA).
proposed_reconstructed_transition_archit.state_3: Dynamic recovery operator: exponential restoration function F_recov(t) = F_end + (F_base - F_end)*(1 - exp(-t / tau_recov)) accounting for measurement delay.
proposed_reconstructed_transition_archit.state_4: Task-specific biomechanical transfer: mapping from multi-joint cyclic torque to isometric joint force constraint.
